cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Supportive Rage
cards.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. You've spilled paint on my sofa. Stay there; I'll get a cloth. We can fix this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the carpet too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Keep blotting. You're doing well. That carpet was my birthday present.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cloth's spreading it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're right. Good catch. Take my clean shirt. I am absolutely furious, but you are not tackling this alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For a wedding cake, we weigh the flour. Please put that mug down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's quicker. I've used three mugs already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. Show me the mug, and I'll weigh one mugful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used three different mugs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Please fetch all three. Apparently we're measuring the crockery before we can measure the flour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm tuning this piano. Please leave the keys alone while I listen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm checking the sticky ones so you can fix those too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Mark them with these little stickers. Silently, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done. Shall I peel them off so you can play?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One at a time. After I reach each key. We've nearly invented a system.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the birthday lunch you really want. I'll drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The seaside place. We'd lose your deposit here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forty pounds wasted. Fine. You love the sea; let's make a day of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it. They need another forty now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another forty? Eighty pounds before a bloody sandwich. Give me the number. You're getting your sea view. Ask for a window; you deserve one.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Terms and Conditions
cards.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. I'll lend you the ladder for two lifts to the station.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only need it for five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. One lift, then. And tell your wife my roses have improved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just pay you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five pounds. Three if you say we're still friends when you hand it over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll accept your apology for missing my birthday if I get first choice of Christmas dates.

cards.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.text: Could you hold this shelf bracket against the holes? It keeps slipping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Briefly. I'm dressed for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you turn that top screw once? Then you can let go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's holding. The other screws are already lined up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just tighten those, then? And slide the shelf onto it to check. I'll get your coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you pinch these bouquet stems together? My wedding ribbon keeps sliding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got them. You need wire underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you twist this bit round, just where your fingers are?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. That sharp end will snag the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tuck it in and wind the ribbon over it? One little bow would hide everything. I'll hold the scissors.
